findings.summary: Break-glass SILENCED the five opt-in guards, and did so even under a global escalation to block, while its own docstring asserted it could not silence anything. The branch returned _DEFAULT_MODES directly, skipping the global-env layer and landing on the new off defaults.

emit() logged the DEMOTED mode, zeroing gate_yield's blocks column — which guard_response.md, the one instrument that distinguishes complying with a block from routing around it, counts. Two identical sessions differing only by break-glass produced 2 blocks and 2 UNACCOUNTED rows versus a file never written at all: the record read cleanest exactly where every block was bypassed.

TDD_PLAYBOOK_HOOK_MODE=off was STILL silently ignored at HEAD — the exact defect break-glass was introduced to fix. A third env var was added beside the broken one rather than fixing the swallow, so an operator who types the documented-looking value still gets a silent non-effect.

red_lock is a PRODUCER: it writes active-lock.json and then announces via emit(). Moving it to default-off left the lock created and the agent never told, so the still-BLOCKING testlock hard-stopped edits to files nothing had announced as read-only. Proven in a scratch repo: zero stderr, a real lock on disk, then test_lock_guard exit 2. A regression introduced by the retirement itself.

install_into_repo --doctor keyed its standing-demotion check on startswith('TDD_PLAYBOOK_HOOK'), so TDD_PLAYBOOK_BREAK_GLASS — a strictly WIDER switch that demotes all four blocking gates — was invisible, while a single per-hook demotion was reported. The 2026-07-28 'hole 2' reopened by a wider knob.

--class became required while five of six in-product hints still printed the class-less command that now exits 2, including test_lock_guard's block message — the most-seen instruction in the product. The previous commit CLAIMED that file was updated; the edit had silently not landed.

The gate_yield header migration sat AFTER the no-events early return, so on a quiet cycle — exactly how the header went stale — it never ran. Its row predicate was narrower than parse_md_rows', silently dropping a non-2026 row and the operator's DEMOTION JOURNAL note; it truncated in place with no temp+rename; and it shipped with no planted test, against this repo's own release rule.

README's hook tiers named three now-opt-in guards as 'advisory default warn' and omitted two entirely; break-glass appeared in ZERO documentation and was absent from the BLOCKING message shown at the moment of need; HACK_CATALOG named overmock/exitcode/exhaustive as the live defense for H9/H13/H14 when none fires on a default install; CLAUDE.md's downstream-refresh prompt listed the wrong guard set.

The break-glass banner printed 'this gate would normally BLOCK' unconditionally whenever the switch was set, so an advisory gate that merely warned said it too — the banner was a proxy for the switch being set rather than a statement about the gate.
